Second, the reinvestment is net of withholding you cannot reclaim (see tax-withholding), so the holder's return is structurally below a direct shareholder's; s. 2.5.1.2 lists 'retained dividends' among the reasons returns will differ. No procedure exists for challenging a missing or mis-sized multiplier increase; clause XV makes the issuer's calculations final and binding save manifest error, and clause XVII excludes liability for calculation errors. This quote is the issuer's own docs page rather than the prospectus because the prospectus nowhere describes the dividend mechanism from the holder's point of view; the two are consistent.

whatIf.outcome: Tax is withheld upstream and you cannot reclaim it. Dividends are reinvested net of withholding — Kraken states the rebase is computed on the net dividend after 30% US withholding tax — and the issuer and paying agent have a right but no duty to deduct further taxes from your payments, with no compensation. The issuer, not you, is the entity of record: it reports your holding and payments to the Jersey Comptroller under FATCA and CRS.
whatIf.quote: The Issuer and the Paying Account Provider shall have the right, but not the duty, to withhold or deduct from any amounts otherwise payable to the Investor such amount as is necessary for the payment of such taxes, duties, fees and/or charges. Investors shall not be entitled to receive amounts to compensate for any amount so withheld or deducted.
whatIf.locator: p. 122, Terms and Conditions clause XII 'Taxation'
whatIf.note: The rate is disclosed only at venue level: Kraken's support FAQ (read 2026-09-18) states 'The rebasing calculation: Net Dividend (after 30% US withholding tax) divided by the closing price of the underlying share on the prior day' — the statutory US non-resident rate, i.e. no treaty relief is passed to holders, while the issuer's own docs say only 'net of applicable withholding taxes'. Nothing in the documents gives a holder treaty access, a tax voucher, a withholding certificate or a reclaim route, and the taxpayer of record is the issuer or its custodian; the issuer separately notes it 'may be subject to local withholding taxes in respect of income or gains derived in certain countries, and in particular from underlying investments'. Reporting: the Issuer 'is considered a Jersey resident financial institution' obliged to report certain holdings and payments to the States of Jersey Comptroller of Revenue under the US-Jersey IGA, onward-reported to the United States, and to identify and report 'reportable accounts' under the Jersey CRS Regulations, which may be passed to the competent authority where the holder is resident; where an investor fails to provide requested information the Issuer 'may be obliged, and/or reserves the right, to take any action and/or pursue all remedies at its disposal'. The issuer itself is taxed in Jersey at 0% and holds International Services Entity status for GST. The Issuer may also redeem all outstanding securities early 'for certain tax reasons' (s. 2.6.5). Jersey imposes no stamp duty on transfers between living persons but charges up to 0.75% on grants of probate.

whatIf.outcome: The multiplier is produced by an automated mechanism fed by oracles the Tokenizer operates, expressly 'without involvement of the Issuer', and the issuer's calculations are final and binding on you save manifest error or wilful misconduct. A manifest error can be corrected by amendment without your consent. Nothing allocates the cost of trades done at a wrong multiplier, and no compensation is promised.
whatIf.quote: The Recalculation Value is being fetched by data oracles operated by the Tokenizer, or third parties based on the Reference Source on any Recalculation Event and automatically fed into the Product’s smart contract, where the Recalculation and the reallocation of securities is being conducted automatically without involvement of the Issuer.
whatIf.locator: p. 116, Terms and Conditions clause VI. vi (identical text at s. 3.16, p. 80)
whatIf.note: Correction machinery: clause XV — 'All calculations, decisions and determinations made by the Issuer shall (save in the case of manifest error or wilful misconduct) be final and binding on the Investors' — and clause XXVII, which allows amendment without holder consent 'for the purpose of correcting a manifest error'; clause XVII removes responsibility 'for any errors or omissions in the calculation of any amount'. Who holds the key matters here: per the dossier, the scaledUiAmountConfig authority on all 165 xStocks mints is S7vYFFWH6BjJyEsdrPQpqpYTqLTrPRK6KW3VwsJuRaS, a plain hot wallet (owner 11111111111111111111111111111111, space 0) that signs Token-2022 instructions at transaction level with no multisig program in the transaction — one unilateral signature restates every holder's displayed balance on every mint, and it is a different key from the mint, freeze/pause and permanent-delegate authorities. The only published mitigation is procedural and aimed at venues, not holders: 'Trading venues and protocols are advised to pause interactions with the affected token for a brief window around each activation timestamp to prevent unexpected settlement behavior' (xStocks docs). Who bears trades executed at a wrong or late multiplier is addressed nowhere in the prospectus, the docs, Kraken's pages or the Terms of Service.

whatIf.outcome: This case cannot arise for xStocks as constituted: every underlying is an already-listed equity or ETF, so there is no pre-IPO holding, no liquidity-event waterfall and no possibility of the issuer never receiving proceeds.
whatIf.locator: p. 90, s. 4.6 'Information concerning the Underlying' and s. 4.6.1 'Equity instruments as Underlying'
whatIf.note: The prospectus requires that 'The Underlyings must be in the form of book-entry securities' and, for equities, instruments 'that are admitted to trading on a stock market that is located in a jurisdiction which is an ordinary member of the International Organisation of Securities Commissions'; the continuing-offer annex lists listed equities and ETFs with CH-prefixed ISINs and the word 'SpaceX' does not appear anywhere in the document. The nearest analogues for an underlying that stops existing on its own terms are clause IX.iii (delisting — termination at fair market value) and clause IX.iv (underlyings with a fixed maturity date — same maturity, Issuer Call Option, or replacement of the underlying at the issuer's sole discretion). Caveat: each product's underlying is fixed by its Final Terms, not by the Base Prospectus, so if Backed were to list a private-company product under the same programme this answer would have to be revisited.

whatIf.outcome: You cannot vote and you get no shareholder information. The prospectus excludes all shareholder rights, and the issuer's docs and Kraken's disclosure repeat it. The issuer holds the shares as collateral and keeps the voting rights until enforcement; the custodian handles corporate actions on the issuer's instruction, and there is no proxy or pass-through to token holders.
whatIf.quote: Most importantly, the Investors' respective creditors' rights do not consist of any shareholders' rights; thus, excluding all rights of attendance, dividend payments, other participation rights or voting rights at a general assembly of the Issuer or any issuers of Underlyings/Underlying Components or any issuers of the Collateral or other entities.
whatIf.locator: p. 83, s. 4.1.6 'Rights attached to the Securities' (repeated in Terms and Conditions clause III)
searched: web search: Kraken support xStocks voting instructions shareholder meeting
whatIf.note: s. 2.5.2.4 adds that the product 'does not constitute a claim to receive information from the respective issuer or sponsor of the Underlying and does not entitle the Investor to exercise voting rights or to receive distributions' (risk rating: high). Who does vote: the custodian 'is, together and subject to instructions by the Issuer, responsible for all matters in connection with corporate actions in the Underlyings' (p. 67), and under the US and UK account control agreements, until an exclusive-control or enforcement notice, 'the Issuer shall remain entitled to (i) exercise voting and/or consent rights with respect to the financial assets and the Securities Account'. Unverified contrary report: crypto.news (7 August 2026) reports that Backed's custody terms were updated to bind it to follow token-holder voting instructions submitted through Kraken accounts and recorded on Ink. No primary source for that was found — the Base Prospectus approved 8 May 2026, the xStocks docs ('do not convey shareholder rights, such as voting rights'), Kraken's live risk disclosure and Kraken's support FAQ ('xStocks do not confer shareholder rights like voting') all still say there is no vote as at 2026-09-18 — so it is recorded here as unverified and not relied on. If it is real, it would change this answer and the dossier's voting field.

whatIf.outcome: Reclassification or illegality is the issuer's exit, not yours: it may terminate the whole product under the Regulatory Call and cash you out, and the prospectus warns that a regulatory change could force it to discontinue operations entirely, 'includ[ing] a risk of total loss for the investors'. Where the token is banned in your own jurisdiction the risk is expressly yours. The offering itself rests on an approval that expires on 7 May 2027 unless renewed.
whatIf.quote: Therefore, it cannot be ruled out that negative effects of a change in the regulatory environment will result in the Issuer no longer being able to operate its business operations economically and having to discontinue them as whole or partially. This includes a risk of total loss for the investors.
whatIf.locator: p. 32, s. 2.3.3.1 'Changes of the Regulatory Environment'
whatIf.note: Parallel clauses: s. 2.4.2.3 warns new rules 'may, inter alia, result in substantial modifications of the smart contracts and/or the issuance of tokenized securities, including its termination and the loss of the investment for the Investors'; clause VI.iii.b is the Regulatory Call; clause XXII.i.2 makes a regulator forcing the issuer to cease activity a Realization Event. The regulatory basis is narrower than it looks: the Base Prospectus is FMA-approved and passported into 29 EEA states but is 'valid until the expiry on 7 May 2027', after which the obligation to supplement ceases; the Swiss offering is limited to professional investors; the Jersey consents expressly do not confer regulated status, and 'The Issuer is not required to be licensed, registered, or authorized under any current securities, commodities or banking laws of its jurisdiction of incorporation and will operate without supervision by any authority in any jurisdiction' (s. 2.6.2). The issuer's docs concede classification risk elsewhere: 'other jurisdictions may classify them differently, including as crypto assets'. Holder-side risk is allocated to the holder: 'Investors bear the risk of the permissibility of the purchase of any Products by themselves' (s. 2.2.2), and a holder in a jurisdiction that bans the instrument keeps a token they may be unable to redeem (see change-jurisdiction).

whatIf.outcome: Jersey law and the non-exclusive jurisdiction of the Jersey courts, against an SPV with £100 of share capital that the prospectus says is not profitable and may be unable to continue as a going concern, with no guarantee from Kraken or its parent. You are limited to damages and cannot obtain specific performance; Backed's Terms of Service cap its cumulative liability at CHF 100 for users who have paid it nothing. No arbitration clause and no class-action waiver was found — and no collective-redress mechanism is offered either.
whatIf.quote: The Base Prospectus, the Products issued, and the rights and obligations of the Issuer and each of the holders of the Products under the Base Prospectus shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of Jersey.
whatIf.locator: p. 129, Terms and Conditions clause XXVIII 'Governing Law and Jurisdiction'
whatIf.note: The forum is split by layer: service-provider agreements carry their own law and forum (Swiss, New York, England and Wales, Florida, California), and the Registration Agreement — the instrument that governs the token itself, including loss and cancellation — is Swiss law, with the cancellation route running before a single judge in Zug. Remedies: clause XVII, 'Investors are entitled to damages only (if any) and are not entitled to the remedy of specific performance in respect of a Product', and no party is liable for indirect or consequential damages. Backed's Terms of Service repeat the Jersey forum and add 'USERS MAY ONLY BRING CLAIMS RELATING TO ASSETS THEY DIRECTLY HOLD AND CONTROL', a maximum cumulative liability of the fees paid in the preceding six months, and 'IF YOU HAVE NOT MADE ANY PAYMENTS TO BACKED ASSETS FOR THE USE OF THE SERVICES, THEN BACKED ASSETS'S MAXIMUM CUMULATIVE LIABILITY TO YOU SHALL NOT EXCEED CHF 100' — a secondary-market holder has typically paid the issuer nothing. Substance of the defendant: £100 share capital, USD 6,075,434.74 of parent shareholder loans as at 31 December 2025, no credit rating, no government or agency insurance or guarantee, and no Payward/PEL guarantee. No precedent was found: CourtListener returns no opinions or dockets for 'xStocks', none for this issuer under 'Backed Assets' or 'Backed Finance', and nothing for 'tracker certificate' or 'ledger-based securities' as a ledger-based-security dispute; the prospectus reports no proceedings against the issuer in the preceding 12 months.
